newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' 91-day Treasury bill down to 11.526.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' 91-day Treasury bill down to 11.526.

text.p: The Philippines' 91-day Treasury bill rate slipped to an average of 11.526 percent from last week's 11.587, the Bureau of Treasury reported on Monday.
The 364-day bill likewise moved down to an average of 12.701 percent from 12.754.
The 182-day bill bucked the trend with the average slightly rising to 11.930 from 11.928.
Monday's regular auction drew tenders worth 8.780 billion pesos, of which 5.0 billion pesos were awarded.

Dealers said the T-bill auction had less bids compared to previous sessions because banks had been using their pesos to build their dollar reserves on expectations the peso would depreciate to contain the country's widening trade deficit.

Also, they say banks are not aggressively positioning in T-bills because interest rates may have seen the bottom for this year even if inflation had come down to 4.4 percent in September from 7.9 in August.
"Though inflation had come down, there is no sign from the Central Bank it wants interest rates to go down further," one dealer said.
A drop in the Central Bank's rates are seen to fuel further speculation in the foreign exchange market, traders said.
The Central Bank had not changed its overnight lending and borrowing rates of 13.0 and 11.0 percent respectively.
The 364-day bills continued to attract the most number of bids at 4.750 billion pesos, of which 2.5 billion pesos were accepted.
Dealers said banks prefer the 364-day bills because it offered the most attractive yield. The Bureau of Treasury had already increased its offer size for these bills by 500 million pesos.
The 91-day bill, which sold 1.0 billion pesos worth, had the next highest number of tenders at 2.45 billion pesos.

The 182-day bill only had bids of 1.580 billion pesos with 1.500 billion pesos were awarded. Dealers said the 182-day bill's yield premium over the 91-day bill had become narrower and thus, more banks shifted to 91-day bills.
